methods: Fresh source review of active error boundary, API wrappers, worker/runtime, admin portals and snapshot SQL.
Read current and legacy operational guides; no peer reports consulted.
Read permitted aggregate live-service baseline and root budget reconciliation; no private rows or logs retrieved.
Ran npm run test:run -- src/__tests__/lib/admin-api.test.ts supabase/tests/jobvance-admin.test.ts supabase/tests/job-loop-scheduler-ticket.test.ts --maxWorkers=4: 3 files and 24 tests passed.
not_tested: Direct production browser/admin session or private production logs.
Production scheduler dispatch, failure injection, provider invoice reconciliation, restoration or rollback rehearsal.
Paid provider calls, incident response timing and real candidate reproduction.

criteria.name: Error signal coverage and safe correlation
criteria.evidence: job-loop-worker/index.ts:17,23 records exception type only; runtime.ts:87-89 has safe codes but no correlation reference; ErrorBoundary.tsx:27 logs full objects.

criteria.name: Diagnosis, reproduction and support intake
criteria.evidence: Selected audited support reads, versioned updates and account-change fencing exist; AdminRun exposes no reason or recovery class.

criteria.name: Severity, noise and actionable health
criteria.evidence: Partial status includes deliberate unavailable lanes; scheduler readiness is configuration-based and freshness has no documented operational threshold.

criteria.name: Containment, retry and spend safety
criteria.evidence: Scoped owner controls, durable runs, consent, idempotency and retained uncertain usage are source-confirmed; aggregate committed ledger reconciles.

criteria.name: Release, rollback and operator rehearsal
criteria.evidence: Integrated guide describes additive rollback and preservation, but OPERATIONS.md commands and provider/support guidance conflict with current admin guide; rehearsal unverified.

strengths: Support text opens only by explicit staff selection; reads and versioned writes are audited and private view state is cleared on close/account change.
Owner controls enforce optimistic configuration saves and identify key validity separately from successful model execution.
Uncertain paid calls retain reservations and are not silently retried; saved work survives dispatch failures.
A bounded local boundary check passed 24 tests; no complete-suite rerun was needed.

findings.problem: Safe error responses lose machine-readable context between candidate failures, worker failures and operator summaries; raw browser console objects are not a safe diagnostic contract.

evidence.detail: Asynchronous scheduler and stage catch handlers log only exception type; ordinary stage logging is also at line23.
Known errors return code/message; unexpected errors retain only type and no event reference.
The client constructs a generic Error from public message text, discarding response code.
Writes error and component errorInfo objects to browser console without an allowlisted diagnostic contract.

findings.recommendation: Create a minimal server-issued event reference and allowlisted operation, release, phase, error code, timestamp and recovery class. Persist safe coded run state. Offer explicit copy-diagnostics UI; exclude CV/vacancy text, email, full URLs, tokens, receipt secrets and arbitrary exception messages. Preserve the local check's no-silent-upload boundary.
acceptance_criteria: A fictional failure can be joined from copied client reference to a worker event and authorized run summary.
Diagnostic privacy tests with canary CV text, emails, URLs and receipt secrets find none in copied or stored payloads.
Existing authorization, account-change fencing and support receipt secrecy continue to pass.
findings.cost_effect: Engineering plus small bounded storage on the existing stack; no new service required.

findings.problem: Expected unavailable coverage and real execution faults share partial status; operator run summaries provide no safe cause, and completed/failed-only metrics cannot explain usable partial work.

evidence.detail: Adds an explicitly blocked LinkedIn lane because no authorized integration exists; line271 makes any blocked/partial/not_connected lane produce overall partial.
AdminRun includes identity, status, phase, provider/model and dates, without diagnostic reason or recovery class.
Completed preparation excludes partial, blocked and failed; lines37-38 and68-74 count only completed/failed for those labeled measures.
Permitted aggregate has three partial runs and prepared packets. This does not establish three incidents or their private causes.

findings.recommendation: Keep honest lane limits but add outcome dimensions for usable artifact, expected unavailable lane, retriable fault, input/consent hold and uncertain paid operation. Expose redacted reasons and actions in admin; do not count every partial as success.
acceptance_criteria: Fictional manual success with unavailable LinkedIn, actual feed failure and uncertain model call produce distinct operator actions.
Admin shows partial/blocked reasons without source text or private messages.
Metric definitions distinguish prepared usable artifacts from full coverage and execution failure.
findings.cost_effect: Engineering only; reduces time wasted investigating expected limitations.

findings.problem: Readiness is configuration-based; existing timestamps and queue counts require the founder to infer stale dispatch without a documented freshness rule.

evidence.detail: Scheduler ready checks enabled state, JOB_LOOP_ENABLED and required server configuration; message explicitly leaves future successful dispatch unverified.
Shows enabled/not-ready/paused state with due schedules and stale leases.
Snapshot exposes last_dispatch_at, due schedules and stale leases; this is useful health input, not dispatch-success proof.

findings.recommendation: Add a simple existing-dashboard health rule when enabled and work is due: stale dispatch, repeated coded failures or increasing stale leases. Start with a hypothesis of three five-minute ticks and calibrate in pilot. Group repeats; keep paused, idle and expected unavailable states quiet.
acceptance_criteria: Fixed-time tests distinguish paused, idle, stale, degraded and recovered states.
A repeated identical fault produces one grouped issue with occurrence count and last seen.
No incident is inferred solely from configuration readiness or a partial status.
findings.cost_effect: Existing dashboard first; no paid monitoring or paging service needed.

findings.problem: Conflicting operational guides can direct a founder to obsolete commands or unsafe broad troubleshooting; containment and rollback procedures lack a verified end-to-end rehearsal.

evidence.detail: Legacy guide lists scripts absent from current package.json, including db:migrate, type-check and test:e2e, and recommends localStorage.clear for sessions.
Directs daily support review through Table Editor; line34 describes paid adapters as unavailable despite current admin guide's configured paid route.
Current portal supports selected audited message review; lines46-50 document owner controls and safe refresh on uncertain saves.
Router toggle controls OpenRouter specifically; scheduler pause is not represented as a universal in-flight cancellation.
No production restoration, scoped pause or rollback rehearsal was performed in this audit.

findings.recommendation: Redirect legacy docs to one current founder runbook. Describe scheduler pause, route-specific provider disablement, in-flight limits and uncertainty reconciliation. Rehearse preservation of drafts/history/holds, prior frontend rollback and compatible worker/schema readback using isolated fictional data. Require exact reviewed release artifact, relevant regressions and a fictional upload-approve-download smoke test before release. Limit automatic action to classification/deduplication and explicitly idempotent retries; no automatic patches, deploys, cap increases, approvals, erasure or uncertain-call replays.
acceptance_criteria: Every documented script exists and provider/support instructions match the active product.
A founder can classify a synthetic bug, pause the right scope, preserve uncertain reservations and verify recovery without copying private text.
A saved frontend can be restored with additive schema compatibility; recurring work resumes only after worker/source/readback checks.
The incident record includes scope, evidence, owner, severity, reproduction, release, rollback condition and verification.
findings.cost_effect: Engineering only; avoids new platform cost and unsupported recovery-time promises.

open_questions: Which recent partial runs contain usable approved artifacts versus an actual failed operation? Aggregate data cannot answer and no private rows were inspected.
Has the founder completed a fictional scoped pause/rollback/restore drill on the current contract?
Who owns daily triage and what response cadence can the pilot honestly sustain?
When can the retained uncertain administrative reservation be reconciled against provider records without assuming zero cost?
do_not_build_now: Sentry or another error platform solely for enterprise appearance; first define a redacted diagnostic contract.
Session replay, raw console uploads or collection of CV/vacancy text for debugging.
Autonomous patches/deploys, automatic cap increases, approval changes, erasure or uncertain paid-call retries.
Separate persona-specific triage products, a dedicated incident platform or 24/7 paging for a ten-user pilot.
